newsitem.title: SPAIN: FORECAST - Bank of Spain seen holding key rate Tues.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Bank of Spain seen holding key rate Tues.

text.p: The Bank of Spain will leave its key money market rate unchanged at 5.25 percent at its repurchase agreement on Tuesday, economists and traders said on Monday.

A Reuter poll conducted on Monday among 10 financial analysts and dealers showed all ruled out a monetary easing tomorrow, despite a general consensus that the Spanish central bank still has scope to cut its rate.
European financial market weakness due to worries on the timetable of the European economic and monetary Union (EMU) was suggesting a cautious monetary approach, analysts added.

But they remained convinced that at the next central bank's repo, after the June 13 announcement of the Spanish May CPI, the monetary authority could move forward and cut its official rate for the fifth time this year.

"Given speculation over EMU, the Bank of Spain will hold the rate, although with quieter markets, another 25-basis-points cut is likely in the next three months," said Fernando Mazon, analyst at ADISA Catalunya.
He stressed that in real terms Spanish interest rates are higher than previously after inflation rate fell to a fresh record low of 1.7 percent year-on-year in April.
In May, economists are expecting the CPI rate to fall to around 1.5 percent.
"Now the inflation rate is falling faster than interest rates," said Mazon.
The Bank of Spain last cut rates on May 16 to 5.25 percent,
